_comment: Copy to the project root as .frontend-audit.json (or pass --config). Globs are relative to the project root; first matching domain wins. Start from `node scripts/domain-deps.mjs . --suggest-config` and group folders into the business capabilities your users name (the names below are placeholders for a generic back office): pages, components and the composables that serve them belong together.
_comment_shell: App chrome: layouts, middleware, plugins, the home page, the project hub. Shell may depend on coreDomains without a finding.
_comment_shared: Domain-free code: UI primitives, formatting, the HTTP client, error contract.
_comment_coreDomains: Domains that the shell legitimately depends on (session, identity, tenant). Not reported as shell-depends-on-domain.
_comment_coreStores: Store ids expected to be used from everywhere (not reported as store-shared-across-domains).
_comment_publicRoutes: Pages that need no guard (login, callbacks, public status pages).
_comment_authPatterns: Extra function names that count as an authorization check in Next.js Server Actions and Route Handlers.
_comment_exclude: 1.3: project-relative globs or bare directories left out of every tool (generated code, nested packages, build artifacts). Invalid patterns (absolute, .., catch-all) stop the tool; the report lists what was excluded.
_comment_dependencies: 1.3: dependency policy between business domains. Pairs outside `allowed` are forbidden-dependency (runtime high, type-only low); `exceptions` stay visible as architecture-exception with their counts; a cycle allowed in both directions is allowed-cycle, not a violation.

exceptions.reason: the project client lives in sales until it moves to projects

_comment_budgets: Gzip KB budgets for bundle-budget.mjs; null disables a metric.
